name: Reality alignment and splitting
summary: Correcting how realities sit on the design: entering a transformation matrix, marking realities as correctly aligned, aligning the rest automatically, viewing several realities as one walkthrough, and splitting a multi-image reality into one reality per image.

roles.note: Every reality route, including the ones that change data, checks only view-project. The web screens for these tools sit under internal routes (tm-viewer, kp-alignment).

requirements.title: Splitting a reality makes one reality per image
requirements.statement: Splitting a reality with two or more images creates, for each image, a new capture, job and reality on the same snapshot with the same status, placed on the structure's default design. The original reality becomes inactive. Inactive realities and single-image realities can't be split. Pinpoints, the snapshot and the structure's capture count are refreshed afterwards.
requirements.rationale: (Current behaviour) The mode check meant to limit splitting to 360 Image and Phone Image always passes, so any active or in-review reality with several images is accepted.

requirements.title: Enter a transformation matrix for a reality
requirements.statement: Users can enter a 4x4 transformation matrix (16 numbers) for a reality to correct its alignment. Anything other than 16 numbers is rejected. Saving it makes it the reality's active matrix for that target and deactivates the others.
requirements.rationale: Current code matches the PRD's 16-number rule and rejection.

requirements.title: Walk through several realities, and align the rest from the good ones
requirements.statement: Users can pick several realities from the type dropdown and see their walkthroughs together. They can mark the realities that are correctly aligned, then start an alignment that aligns the remaining ones from those.
requirements.rationale: PRD-only. An internal transformation-matrix registration screen exists (tm-viewer), but multi-select walkthroughs, marking realities as aligned and automatic alignment were not confirmed in the code read.
